commitResults.messageBody:
Phone validation rejects country-code notation and separators while
accepting numbers of any length. Allow an optional leading plus and
single spaces or hyphens between digits, and cap numbers at 15 digits.

contacts. Document the rules for commands and saved data, including the
need to correct older records exceeding the limit before loading.

Address the format and upper-bound problems in issue #147.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test international phone formats and digit limits
commitResults.messageBody:

through add and edit commands. Verify that saved phone formatting
survives a JSON round trip and reject oversized stored numbers.

Replace invalid-phone examples that become valid under the new rules.
Use a maximally formatted 15-digit number in the UI layout test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a zero immediately after the phone plus sign
commitResults.messageBody:
International phone input accepts a leading zero after + even though
country codes start with 1 through 9. Reject that form while preserving
leading zeros in local numbers without +.

Explain the distinction in validation feedback and the User Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test leading zeros in phone number formats

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null records in saved lists
commitResults.messageBody:
Null entries in saved lists bypass storage error handling and prevent
startup. Reject them as invalid records so startup can use its existing
empty-address-book fallback.

Preserve support for missing optional job and application lists.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test loading null records in saved lists
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover null entries in applicant, job, and application lists through the
storage API. Require the normal loading exception and verify that a
failed read leaves the saved file unchanged.

This guards the malformed-record cases reported in #148.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject root-level null in saved JSON files
commitResults.messageBody:
A JSON null deserializes successfully but cannot represent loaded data
or preferences. Wrapping that result in an optional crashes startup.

Report it as a loading error so both storage consumers use their
existing recovery paths instead of treating the file as missing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test loading root-level null JSON files
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover saved data and preferences containing only null. Require a
loading error in both cases and verify that reading preserves the
invalid content for diagnosis.

These cases extend the malformed-file coverage for #148.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null GUI settings when loading preferences
commitResults.messageBody:
Explicit null GUI settings pass deserialization but fail when the model
copies preferences. Reject these preferences at the storage boundary
so startup uses its existing default-preferences fallback.

Keep default GUI settings when the field is omitted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test loading null GUI settings
commitResults.messageBody:

reading leaves the preferences file unchanged.

The existing missing-field test continues to cover default settings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recognize Java whitespace at option boundaries
commitResults.messageBody:
Unicode separators before an option can be stored as part of the
preceding value, while separators after an option can hide that option.
This lets addj silently save a description as part of the job role.

Use the same Java whitespace definition for option boundaries and value
trimming. Document the accepted separators without changing which
characters count as whitespace.

Refs #185

commitResults.messageTitle: Test Unicode whitespace at option boundaries
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover the addj reproduction from #185 and Unicode separators around
options and values, including indexed preambles and flag options.

Require unknown and duplicate options to remain errors, and preserve
characters outside the Java whitespace definition inside values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow adjacent punctuation in email local parts
commitResults.messageBody:
Addresses such as alice__lee@example.com meet the stated local-part
rules but are rejected because punctuation must alternate with
alphanumeric groups.

Allow adjacent supported punctuation while retaining alphanumeric
boundaries and rejecting consecutive periods. Clarify the validation
message and User Guide so they describe the accepted addresses.

Refs #168

commitResults.messageTitle: Test adjacent punctuation in email local parts
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover repeated and mixed local-part punctuation in email validation
and the add and edit parsers. Keep invalid boundaries and consecutive
periods rejected, including periods next to other punctuation.

Check that the 254-character limit still applies to punctuation runs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve Unicode code points in avatar initials
commitResults.messageBody:
Applicant and job avatars split supplementary characters into isolated
UTF-16 surrogates. Extract each initial as a complete code point so
names accepted by the model display correctly in the detail panels.

Count job initials by words rather than UTF-16 length to retain both
initials when the first character occupies two code units. Document
the avatar behavior in the Developer Guide.

Refs #186

commitResults.messageTitle: Test supplementary Unicode avatar initials
commitResults.messageBody:
Check applicant and job detail labels with supplementary characters
in either initial position and in single-word names and roles.

Cover uppercase conversion and the two-word limit alongside ordinary
initials so Unicode support preserves the existing avatar behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe supported fields in editj usage
commitResults.messageBody:
The editj parser accepts description edits and preserves omitted fields,
but its usage text presents the role as required and omits descriptions.
This hides supported edits when users encounter malformed input.

Show both optional fields, the requirement to supply at least one, and
all aliases. Explain omitted-field preservation and align nearby parser
documentation with the implemented behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test editj description-error guidance
commitResults.messageBody:

to explain optional role and description edits, omitted-field behavior,
and supported aliases.

Existing parser and command tests cover successful edits; this checks
that the user-facing recovery instructions describe those capabilities.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix email validation and long option parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
Long emails and option tokens can overflow the stack or delay command
execution. Valid Punycode domains are also rejected.

Reject emails longer than 254 characters, accept consecutive domain
hyphens, and prevent stack overflow when parsing long option tokens.
Keep the production changes focused and cover add and edit parsing with
regression tests. Document the email limit, including its effect on
saved data.

Fixes #164
Fixes #152

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept common punctuation and Unicode in names
commitResults.messageBody:
Applicant names with hyphens, apostrophes, slashes, periods, or accented
letters are rejected, preventing recruiters from recording real names.

Expand name validation to accept common punctuation and Unicode letters,
including combining accents, while retaining the existing letter or
digit requirement for the first character. Apply the shared rules to
adding, editing, and loading applicants without changing stored names.

Add regression tests for command parsing and save/reload behavior, and
document the accepted characters.

Fixes #146

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn when deletion also removes applications
commitResults.messageBody:
Deleting an applicant or job also removes its applications, but users
may overlook this consequence in the command result.

Add an explicit warning after applicant deletion when an application
was removed. Report the actual number of applications removed with a
job, including applications hidden by filters. Keep deletion immediate
and preserve the existing command syntax.

Cover the warnings and deletion counts with regression tests, and
document the feedback behavior.

Fixes #141

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject applicant duplicates regardless of case
commitResults.messageBody:
Capitalization differences let duplicate names and emails bypass
applicant uniqueness checks, creating separate records for the same
contact details.

Compare names and emails without regard to case when checking for
duplicates. Preserve entered spelling and allow applicants to change
their own capitalization. Use the shared duplicate check so adding,
editing, and loading applicants follow the same rules.

Add regression tests for hidden duplicates, capitalization edits, and
saved data. Document that older saves with case-only duplicates must
be corrected before loading.

Fixes #145

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow copying values from detail panels
commitResults.messageBody:
Recruiters cannot copy contact and job details displayed as labels,
forcing them to transcribe values into other applications.

Add a Copy context menu to applicant, application, and job detail
values while preserving the existing layout. Copy the complete current
value and disable the action for empty values. Share the behavior
between panels to keep the change focused.

Document the interaction and add UI tests covering selection changes,
empty values, application status updates, and multiline Unicode text.

Fixes #135

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep long list cards within the available width
commitResults.messageBody:
Long applicant fields and application details expand cards beyond the
list viewport, causing horizontal scrolling and squeezing status badges.

Let the text columns shrink and grow within the available list width.
Keep full values intact, shorten applicant labels, and wrap application
text so the cards remain usable when the window is resized.

Add UI regression tests for long fields at multiple widths and document
how full details remain accessible through record selection.

Fixes #133
Fixes #171

commitResults.messageTitle: Standardize surrounding whitespace in commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Stored job roles ignore Unicode whitespace, but command inputs use
inconsistent normalization. This prevents applications from finding
existing jobs and lets blank roles reach job construction during edits.

Apply one whitespace policy to commands, parameter values, indexes,
searches, and diagnostic messages. Preserve internal field text and case
sensitivity. Reject non-whitespace control characters before execution
so malformed input cannot mutate or persist data.

Remove redundant job-parser normalization and align search word
boundaries with the same whitespace definition. Add regression tests for
Unicode padding, blank values, control characters, application
references, and save/reload behavior. Document the shared input policy.

Fixes #153
Fixes #165

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix native focus dependency in arrow-key test
commitResults.messageBody:
The arrow-key UI test requires the test window to be active even
when the detail pane retains scene focus and scrolls correctly.
This can report a failure when the operating system has not
activated the window.

Assert scene focus ownership while retaining the selection and
scrolling checks. This verifies keyboard routing without depending
on native window activation.

to a copyable label inside it. Requiring the pane itself to own
focus reports a failure even when selection and scrolling work.

Accept focus anywhere within the detail pane while retaining the
selected-job and scrolling checks. This covers child focus without
depending on native window activation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve the previous save when a write fails
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving overwrites the existing file immediately. If the write
stops partway, the previous valid save is already gone and the
next launch cannot read the file.

Let's write the new content beside the save and replace the save
only after that write finishes.

A failed write can then leave the previous save in place.
Replacing a file in its own directory can be done atomically.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject save files with trailing JSON content
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file with two JSON values is read as only the first
value. A later save then overwrites the file and discards the
rest.

Let's reject JSON that still has content after the first value.

Malformed files already fail through the storage error path, so
the extra value is kept on disk instead of being dropped.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep running when the log file cannot be opened
commitResults.messageBody:
A failed file logger reports the error through a logger that
does not exist yet, so startup aborts instead of continuing
with the console logger.

Let's report that failure through the base logger, which
already has a console handler.

Startup can then continue when the log file path is unusable.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Select the next list entry with the arrow keys
commitResults.messageBody:
A long applicant, application, or job list can only be moved
through with the mouse or a view command. The command box
keeps keyboard focus, so the arrow keys do not change the
selected record.

Let's move the selection on the current tab when Up or Down
is pressed, and scroll that record into view.

The detail panel already follows the list selection, and a
single-line command box does not use those keys for editing.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an undo command for the last change
commitResults.messageBody:
Deleting an applicant or job by the wrong index can be
reversed only by retyping the lost record. The detail panel
shows what was removed, but it does not put the record back.

Let's remember the address book from before each change and
restore that copy with undo.

Only commands that change stored records are remembered, so
listing or viewing does not use up the undo.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Update javadocs accordance with the coding standard
Remember a description edit for undo
commitResults.messageBody:
A job edit that changes only the description still compares equal,
because job equality uses the role. Undo then skips that edit and
restores an earlier change instead.

Let's treat different descriptions as a stored change. Job equality
stays based on the role, so the same role cannot be added twice.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep arrow keys for text and detail panes
commitResults.messageBody:
Up and Down are consumed for every focused control, so the result
text and a job description can no longer scroll.

Let's move the list selection only when the command box or a list
has the key. Other controls then keep their own arrow-key behavior.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Update a linked save file in place
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving replaces a symbolic link with a normal file, so later saves
no longer reach the file the link pointed to.

Let's write through an existing link to its target. The permission
test is skipped when that directory cannot be made read-only.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
